target_customer: Knowledge workers and teams that type repetitive text in the browser, with business and enterprise plans as the long-term target
problem: People retype the same emails, replies and notes all day. Text Blaze lets them save snippets and templates with fillable fields and insert them anywhere with a shortcut.
business_model: Freemium Chrome extension with a free tier capped at 20 snippets, paid consumer plan at $2.99 per month and higher priced business plans

founders.name: Dan Barak
prior_employers: Google (product manager, per TextExpander blog via search summary)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2021 names him without background; the Google detail comes from a competitor's blog seen only in a search summary.

founders.name: Scott Fortmann-Roe
prior_employers: Google (product manager, per TextExpander blog via search summary)
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page with no bio.

competitors.name: TextExpander
competitors.what: Established paid text expander for Mac, Windows and browsers

technical_complexity.rationale: A Chrome extension with templating, logic and integrations; moderate engineering for a team of four, with no research risk.

defensibility.rationale: Saved snippet libraries create some lock-in, but text expansion tools are abundant including free open source ones and the free tier is capped, which drives users to alternatives.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying found; the company later added AI Blaze.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in May 2021 reported more than 70,000 users of the Chrome extension with about 70 percent signing up with corporate email addresses and early revenue.

branding.community_and_virality: Trademark TEXT BLAZE registered Feb 2020 to Blaze Today Inc; competitors publish alternative comparison pages naming it.

brand_strength.rationale: Competitors write comparison content against it and it reached 70,000 users by 2021, but no source credits the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Text Blaze grew a Chrome extension to over 70,000 users by May 2021 and raised a 3.3 million dollar seed led by Two Sigma Ventures and Susa Ventures, then kept shipping into AI templates with AI Blaze. No later round or exit was found, so the outcome remains an active small company.
